parsed.elsewhere_quote: So the hypothesis of Lemma 4.1(b) holds, and some ordering of $P\cup N$ has chain value $g\le\frac{S}{2^m-1}$.
parsed.explanation: The objection is locally right: v(B) is defined via the decreasing ordering, yet Lemma 4.1 and Theorem 4.2's proof only produce *some* ordering of P∪N with nested value g, and decreasing order need not achieve it. But the substance of L3.2 survives: the pigeonhole gives a subset (P∪N) and an explicit ordering with nested value ≤ S/(2^{n+1}-1)=T_n, and XY's cut strategy (cut the larger of running piece and b_k, set aside equal pairs, bisect the rest) is order-agnostic — it never uses b_1≥…≥b_r, only sequential processing. So the notation 'b_1≥…≥b_r' is a misprint beside a valid argument; replacing it by 'in the order supplied by Lemma 4.1' repairs it in one sentence.
